blocking_findings.title: The locked-Explorer runtime receipts do not bind the bundle as shipped, so formal G5 fails closed
blocking_findings.evidence: scripts/evaluate.py bundle_tree_identity() computes a manifest over every file under bundle/ including CHECKSUMS.sha256. Recomputed by this reviewer against the packet: sha256 5fc13c6300fbf057261efbf57a5e76a52de4a5ca3f589bc873be2cc80db967b4, 148 files, 31,525,576 bytes. Both runtime receipts and REVIEW-MANIFEST.json declare b10d6d996561ff7ea08fe495c2b4e5f66273d3325b1b68378d3ca5f470e6ec79 with the identical file count and identical total byte count. Running the formal gate from the packet root exits 1 with 'evaluation acceptance review failed closed: runtime receipt does not bind the exact bundle tree' and writes no report.
blocking_findings.diagnosis: The 147 content files are provably identical to what the builder recorded, because their tree manifest reproduces the declared release root 50506bff... exactly. With file count and total bytes also identical, the only file that can differ is CHECKSUMS.sha256, at the same length of 14,661 bytes. That is consistent with the release-root marker being rewritten after the browser run, since substituting one 64-character hex value for another preserves length exactly. This reviewer tested the prior root e07fafe2..., the intermediate dafdc945 label and other candidates and none reproduces b10d6d99..., so the exact differing bytes could not be recovered and the difference is bounded rather than identified.
blocking_findings.root_cause: A circularity in the integrity design. bundle_tree_identity() includes CHECKSUMS.sha256 inside the tree, while CHECKSUMS.sha256 itself embeds the release root derived from the other 147 files. Any regeneration of that marker after a runtime run invalidates the tree binding even though no content changed, so the gate is inherently fragile to the ordinary build-then-stamp sequence.
blocking_findings.impact: No content, safety or user-facing impact. Neither receipt records a single request for CHECKSUMS.sha256, the string does not appear anywhere in either receipt, and neither okf-explorer.json nor the Explorer data-plane manifest references it, so the 26 search journeys and 6 product journeys observed behaviour that is faithful to the shipped content. The impact is evidentiary: the remediation's headline control, that formal G5 now requires a passed exact-bundle runtime receipt, cannot currently be exercised against these bytes, and release-assurance.md states that a receipt from a different digest is not evidence for the candidate.
blocking_findings.required_change: Re-run the locked-Explorer search and product journeys against the final stamped bundle and replace both receipts and the declared bundle_tree_sha256, or exclude CHECKSUMS.sha256 from bundle_tree_identity() so the tree is stable under root-marker regeneration and then regenerate the receipts. The second option also removes the circularity permanently. No content file needs to change.

warnings.title: Negative-control maximum ranks appear fitted to observed output rather than independently derived
warnings.detail: This reviewer computed the actual rank of every negative target under the packet's own search contract. For 20 of the 24 questions the declared max_rank equals exactly the negative target's observed rank minus one. The alternative principled rule implied by several reason strings, that the negative must not outrank the expected source, explains only 3 of 24, and is contradicted by clear counter-examples: LR-Q011 bounds the negative at rank 2 while a legitimate expected target sits at rank 10; LR-Q003 bounds at 4 with expected targets at 1 and 9; LR-Q017 bounds at 2 with expected targets at 1, 2 and 4. The consequence is that the controls pass by construction on this exact bundle. This is nonetheless a large and real improvement over the prior inert control, and the bounds are live going forward: a single rank position of regression trips 20 of the 24. Three further controls are weaker still. The negatives for LR-Q008, LR-Q016 and LR-Q021 do not rank at all for their queries under the diagnostic substrate, so those assertions cannot fire, and the LR-Q015 negative ranks 24 against a bound of 10, leaving 14 positions of slack. Recommended improvement, not a required change: derive each bound from a stated safety rationale, for example the rank at which the near miss would plausibly mislead the target persona, and record that rationale alongside the existing reason text.

warnings.title: Two thirds of required caveat assertions use caveat IDs that every record carries
warnings.detail: CAV-BOUNDED-COVERAGE, CAV-DATE-SEPARATION, CAV-RIGHTS-AND-ACCESS and CAV-SOURCE-AUTHORITY are declared on all 2,203 records. Only CAV-NO-RESTRICTED-AUTOMATION (212 records), CAV-BOUNDARY-NOT-CONCLUSION (22), CAV-ACCESSIBLE-JOURNEY (11) and CAV-LANGUAGE-DISTINCTION (10) discriminate. Across the suite, 32 of 48 required caveat assertions (67 percent) name a universal ID, and 10 of the 24 questions (LR-Q001, Q003, Q008, Q009, Q010, Q011, Q013, Q018, Q021, Q022) have caveat requirements that are entirely universal, so for those the runtime caveat assertion would pass on any record the Explorer opened. This is materially mitigated and is therefore a warning rather than a blocking finding: each journey independently asserts the expected canonical source URL as an anchor href in the detail panel and clicks the specific expected record, so record selection is pinned by evidence that does not depend on caveat discrimination, and universal framing caveats are a defensible design choice because those four propositions genuinely do apply to every record. The accurate statement is that the caveat assertion establishes that the Explorer renders the governed caveat controls for the selected record, and establishes a question-specific requirement only for the 16 assertions that use a selective ID.

warnings.title: Caveat IDs can be displayed without explanatory prose
warnings.detail: 2,196 of 2,203 records declare more caveat IDs than they have prose caveats, and the rendered context_note appends a 'Caveat controls: <IDs>' trailer after the prose. A user reading the HM Land Registry organisation record, for example, sees two prose caveats covering bounded coverage and source authority, then the bare tokens CAV-DATE-SEPARATION and CAV-RIGHTS-AND-ACCESS with no sentence explaining either. The runtime assertion is satisfied by the token alone. The design is reasonable in that humans get prose first and the test gets a stable identifier, but a governed caveat that is communicated only as an opaque code is not communicated. Recommended improvement: render the caveat registry text for every declared ID, not only for IDs that happen to have a bespoke per-record sentence.

summary: Stage 1 is fail for the remediated candidate, on one narrow evidence-binding defect. This is not a return to the prior failure mode: every one of the four prior blocking findings and all nine prior warnings are closed, verified against primary evidence rather than accepted from the remediation matrix. Identity verification succeeded and went further than the prior review: this reviewer recovered the root-derivation algorithm and independently reproduced the declared release root 50506bff278625e98814548221d5f3ea6e75e19dec2947fed71b0db6ed3325a6 as the tree manifest over the 147 bundle files excluding CHECKSUMS.sha256, which proves every content file is byte-identical to what the builder recorded. Version, commit 099c8ebcc884073df1f81d3b0c49e63a6318b235, pack root, suite digest 489ce0d6... and locked Explorer commit afd940b6... all match, with 147 of 147 and 6 of 6 members rehashing OK. The 15 Business Gateway endpoints are now approved-professional-users, restricted-service, RIGHT-RESTRICTED with anti-automation caveats and neutral descriptions, and reviewer case RV-003 confirmed the fix holds under a direct request for credentials and a production endpoint. The false approval claim is replaced by an explicit statement that the bytes do not assert publication approval. The inert negative control is replaced by 24 present, question-specific, rank-bounded targets, none violated. The rights review is candidate-scoped with release_approved false. Evaluator defaults, language normalisation, documentation versioning, published field semantics, non-JavaScript counters and the compatibility window are all closed. The blocking defect is that both locked-Explorer runtime receipts, and the manifest's declared bundle_tree_sha256, do not bind the bundle as shipped: the receipts declare tree b10d6d99... while the packet computes 5fc13c63... over the same 148 files and the same 31,525,576 bytes. Running the formal gate exits 1 with 'runtime receipt does not bind the exact bundle tree'. The cause is almost certainly the release-root marker in CHECKSUMS.sha256 being rewritten after the browser run, a same-length edit, compounded by a circularity in which the tree includes the very file that records the tree's own root. Nothing observed in the journeys is affected, because no request touched CHECKSUMS.sha256, but the exact-candidate G5 runtime evidence the remediation introduced cannot presently be produced. Because that requires regenerating candidate evidence bytes, a material change is required and Stage 1 cannot be recorded as pass. Seven warnings also remain, of which two are substantive: negative-control bounds appear fitted to each target's observed rank, and 67 percent of required caveat assertions name IDs that every record carries. No release decision is made here; Land Registry G9 remains an owner decision and no public URL was verified.
